approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs. It is wired as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` (checks.rs:539). It reads labelled clauses of the `Code survey:` assumptions: `Entry point:` (one or more identifiers), `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:`, `Reuses:` (`Existing code:` is an alias), `Output:` and `Direct check:`. (a) The gate order and stop gate are identifiers and the stop gate is one of the gates. (b) Reuse names an identifier or says 'no existing function'. (c) `Output:` says no new output, names a record kind from a hand-written list pinned by a test to `AnyRecord` and `HistoryRecord`, or names a round-trip token that a criterion also names with a deliverable that can hold the test. (d) Each non-routine behavior criterion has its own `Direct check:` clause by number. The clause has a measurement word (matched by stem), names an entry point, a gate or a planner, producer or model call, and does not measure through a skip switch or an internal-helper read. Negation is local: a negator governs only the item it directly precedes, through a closed list of bridge words, and a list chain such as 'not a skip switch, `skip_probe` or ATHENA_NO_PROBE'. Only the closed field names `no_change` and `no_change_reason` are exempt from the skip-identifier rule. A gate or entry-point name is not exempt. The refusal error names the check, each missing letter and each contradiction, and ends with an example survey held in a new constant `CODE_SURVEY_EXAMPLE` in athena-context, outside the reader brief. The CLI `check-reading` path and the other callers of `check_reading_text` are listed dependents. Round 4 corrects the replay account: a held replay is a Blocker finding and the job ends Rejected. The plan states that, keeps the 30% declaration the criterion fixes, never loosens the check, and puts the conflict to the user as an open question.

The request lists five labels; `Output:` is added so part (c) is required in every reading and 'omits exactly one of (a)-(d)' can be told apart.

decisions.choice: Skip-switch and internal-helper contradictions use local negation (finding 2 answered) and a narrowed exemption (finding 3 answered). verify.rs `clause_words` and `is_negator` (1368, 1378) become `pub(crate)`, visibility only; `NEGATORS` (1261: not, never, cannot, no, nor, neither, none, nothing, unless) and `split_clauses` are unchanged. surveys.rs has its own `measure_segments(text)`. It splits at `;`, at a full stop followed by whitespace or the end, and at line breaks (never at commas, colons or dots inside a token, so `athena.failure-class/1` and `a::b` stay whole), then at the word `but`. Each segment is a vector of whitespace tokens. Per token, `word` is the lowercase form trimmed of backticks, commas, brackets and `()`, and the raw trimmed token is kept for identifier tests. ITEMS: phrase items are two-word windows `skip switch`, `skip flag`, `skip option`, `internal helper`, `private helper` and the three-word `test only switch`/`test-only switch`; identifier items are single tokens by the identifier forms below. NEGATION (the fix for finding 2): an item is negated only when, scanning backwards from its first token, every token passed over is a BRIDGE word or part of another matched item, and a negator is reached before any other word. Negators are `is_negator` plus `without`, `instead`, `refuse`, `refuses`, `refused`, `reject`, `rejects`, `rejected`, `forbid`, `forbids` (local `is_means_negator`). Bridge words are the closed list: a, an, the, any, by, via, using, through, with, reading, read, adding, add, of, as, or, and, nor, to, just, only, for. A comma never breaks the scan. So a chain 'not a skip switch, `skip_probe` or ATHENA_NO_PROBE' and 'never by reading an internal helper or adding a skip switch' are accepted, because each later item follows the negated one through bridge words. A negator that governs a different word does not carry: 'asserts the probe does not run when ATHENA_NO_PROBE=1 is set' (`run`, `when` are not bridge words) and 'counts no model calls using `skip_probe`' (`model`, `calls` are not bridge words) are refused; 'not `skip_probe` but ATHENA_NO_PROBE=1' is refused because `but` ends the segment. IDENTIFIER FORMS on raw tokens: (1) an all-caps token (uppercase, digits, `_`; `=value` trimmed) counts only when one of its `_` parts is NO, SKIP, SKIPPED, DISABLE, DISABLED or BYPASS (ATHENA_NO_PROBE matches; INPUT_FORMS, READING_RULES, MAX_ROUNDS do not); (2) a lowercase identifier or `--flag` counts only when its FIRST part (split on `_` and `-`) is `skip`, `skipped`, `no`, `disable`, `disabled` or `bypass` (skip_probe, disable_probe, --no-probe match; line_no does not). EXEMPTION: only the closed `KNOWN_FIELD_NAMES` = [`no_change`, `no_change_reason`] is exempt. A name listed in `Entry point:`, `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:` or `Reuses:` is NOT exempt. In a `Direct check:` clause a phrase or identifier counts unless negated. In a behavior criterion only the phrase forms count, and only when a means phrase (`through`, `via`, `using`, `by reading`, `by inspecting`, `measured`, `checked`, `verified` or `tested` followed by `by` or `with`) is within 4 words before it in the same segment with no negator governing it. A bare `read` is not a means phrase. A gate named `skip_probe` may sit in the Gate order; the reading is refused only if a Direct check names it un-negated, and the error tells the reader to cite the entry point or another gate, or to reword. Stated limits (doc comment and CHANGELOG): matching is lexical; a name starting `no`, `skip`, `disable` or `bypass` that is not in the closed field-name list is refused in a Direct check unless negated (for example `skip_whitespace`) and must be reworded or left out of the clause; a skip switch named otherwise is not caught; a criterion describing a refusal fixture with 'through a skip switch' is refused and must be reworded.
decisions.reason: `split_clauses` splits on `; : . ,` (verify.rs:1351), which breaks list negation and cuts dotted tokens. `clause_words` keeps `_` inside words, so `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` never match the phrase list; the identifier forms close that gap. The earlier rule let any earlier negator cancel everything after it in the segment, so ordinary skip-switch measurements passed (finding 2). The bridge-word rule keeps the negator tied to the item it governs and still accepts the comma-list wording the guide asks the reader to write. Exempting gate names (the earlier plan) would let a skip switch hide in the Gate order, the loophole closed for Reuses (finding 3); the closed field-name list is smaller and clearer.

risks.risk: Skip-switch matching is lexical. A name starting `no`, `skip`, `disable` or `bypass` (for example `skip_whitespace`) is refused in a Direct check unless negated, even when listed as an entry point or gate (false positive; only `no_change` and `no_change_reason` are exempt). demonstrations.method: `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` builds 10 `ReplayCase` values with the existing `replay_case` helper and `base_checker` pattern (reading.rs ~6466-6545): 3 code readings with the old short survey (newly refused), 3 with the complete survey, 4 docs readings, each built so every later check accepts it. Base and candidate checkers both call `check_reading_text`; the base is applied to the reading with `complete_survey_for` swapped in, the candidate to the reading as built. For each newly refused case it asserts the swapped reading is accepted. The declaration comes from `replay_declaration_of` on a reading whose criterion reads 'expected 30% of newly refused readings, because the check now asks for new required labels that past readings never used'. It asserts `!run.held`, at least 1 newly refused, and `newly_refused * 100 <= total * replay_limit_percent(Some(30))`. A second run whose candidate refuses every code reading asserts `run.held`. This proves the arithmetic only. The real share is the `athena.replay/1` record (`REPLAY_SCHEMA`, records/plan.rs:268), made by `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) during the producer run and again at verification. Expected real outcome, an estimate from HISTORY.txt (176 of 200 commits touch crates/): above 35%, so a held replay is a Blocker finding (verify.rs:500-512) and the job is Rejected (run/verification.rs:437) unless the user first changes the declared share (see the open question). The producer does not loosen anything, does not stop `no_change: blocked`, and gives the measured share, limit and newly refused job ids in each report.
demonstrations.observes: The fixture share is within 30 plus 5 points, the held case holds, at least one case is newly refused, and the swapped readings are accepted by every other check. The producer report carries the real measured share and ids from the loop's feedback.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check newly refused more than the limit of the fixtures, `run.held` is true and the assertion fails. If it refused nothing, the 'at least 1' assertion fails.
